anomalies.observed: On the root sheet the SWD connector J2 (Conn_ARM_SWD_TagConnect_TC2030) drives SWDIO on net NET0012 and SWCLK on net NET0017. The same net labels NET0012 and NET0017 appear on MCU U2 pins 33 (PB12) and 34 (PB13), which are also the wires that feed the DISPLAY hierarchical sheet symbol's pins NET0003 (RES#) and NET0007 (SCL). Thus the debug data/clock nets are merged with the display reset/clock nets on PB12/PB13.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, PB12/PB13/PB14 are reserved for DISP_RES/DISP_SCL/DISP_SDA, while the ARM SWD interface (SWDIO/SWCLK) belongs on the MCU's dedicated debug pins (PA13/PA14), not on the display GPIOs. The debug nets and the display bus nets must be separate.

evidence.quote: Root sheet (PCB.kicad_sch): J2 pin2 'SWDIO' -> NET0012, pin4 'SWCLK' -> NET0017; U2 right column rows 'PB12 33' and 'PB13 34' carry the stacked labels NET0012/NET0017 and are wired to the DISPLAY sheet symbol pins NET0003/NET0007.
DISP_RES: U2 pin 33 (PB12) ...; DISP_SCL: U2 pin 34 (PB13) ...; J1 pins are VCC, GND, ~{RESET}, SWCLK, SWDIO, SWO — a standard ARM debug/programming interface, not a user I/O.

anomalies.impact: The SWD programmer cannot drive the MCU's debug interface (STM32 SWD alternate functions are on PA13/PA14, not PB12/PB13), so programming/debugging fails; simultaneously the DISP_RES and DISP_SCL lines are loaded/shorted by the debug connector, corrupting the OLED bus.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the specification (NFC I2C pull-ups, SSD1306 I2C strapping and charge-pump values, TSC series-R/sampling-C, NRST pull-up), but the SWD connector's SWDIO/SWCLK nets (NET0012/NET0017) are tied to MCU pins PB12/PB13, which are the same pins used for DISP_RES/DISP_SCL, bridging the debug interface with the display bus and putting SWD on the wrong pins.
